title: Tokenized Feature Flags — draft idea log
content:
Name: Tokenized Feature Flags (TFF) — quick brain-dump and rough PRD sketch.

One-line: a tiny, per-response token accounting primitive that lets product teams gate, tier, route, and bill micro-features at inference time without heavyweight config or per-customer forks.

Problem statement:
- We repeatedly need to enable micro-features (e.g., high-fidelity rerank, expanded context window, persona enrichment, post-processing transforms) selectively per request OR per customer tier.
- Current gates are coarse (route entire customer to a model variant or capacity tier) or require custom orchestration. This leads to overprovisioning, complicated rollouts, and poor visibility into incremental cost.

Hypothesis:
- If we expose a tiny, composable token-like budget that can be attached to requests and consumed by runtime features, teams can mix-and-match micro-features on a per-request basis, measure unit economics, and roll them out incrementally.

Goals:
- Provide an SDK + API affordance (TFF) that:
  * Signals which micro-features are enabled for this request and the available budget for them.
  * Is lightweight to evaluate at the serving runtime (O(1) checks), and auditable for billing.
- Make it easy for product and platform to experiment with feature combos without creating new model variants.
- Surface precise metrics (cost per feature, latency delta, error surface) to inform product decisions.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT a replacement for major model variant rollouts or capacity-level SLAs.
- Not intended for high-security gating that depends on separate compliance review processes.

User personas:
- Product manager (PM) — wants to A/B a single micro-feature (e.g., 2x rerank passes) to 10% of users and measure ROI.
- Platform eng — wants low-overhead enforcement and metrics aggregation so they can set sensible defaults.
- Customer success/Enterprise admin — wants to purchase feature bundles that map to token allowances but still needs audit logs.

User stories (examples):
- As a PM, I want to enable ‘re-rank-depth: 2’ for 10% of requests so I can compare accuracy and cost.
- As Platform eng, I want to reject requests that exceed their token allowance, returning a 402-equivalent with clear headers.
- As an Enterprise admin, I want to assign monthly TFF credits to sub-accounts and receive usage reports.

API sketch:
- Request-level: {"tff": [{"feature": "rerank", "units": 1}, {"feature": "persona_enrich", "units": 2}], "tff_token": "acct:abcd:2025-06"} (rough)
- Server behavior: runtime inspects tff array, validates token allowance, atomically reserves units, executes enabled feature hooks in priority order until units exhausted.
- Response: additional headers: X-TFF-Used: rerank=1;persona_enrich=1; X-TFF-Remaining: acct=47
- Console: allow setting default local budgets per route + per-customer override.

Runtime considerations:
- Enforcement must be fast and resilient: a small in-memory allowance check + consistent decrement path. For hosted API we can use a local cache with eventual consistency to avoid RPCs on every request; for Dedicated/Private we integrate with customer-side K/V.
- Hook design: features register a small cost function (units per operation) and a priority. Runtime respects priority and stops invoking features when budget exhausted.
- Fail modes: if a feature can't run due to budget, runtime should optionally run a cheaper fallback (e.g., shallow rerank) and annotate response.

Console UX / Product surfaces:
- Route config: default TFF bundle for route (e.g., free tier: persona=0, rerank=0; pro tier: persona=1, rerank=1).
- Experiment wizard: define cohort %, feature units, period, and target metric (latency, quality).
- Billing page: map consumed units to cost buckets and show cost delta by feature.

Metrics / Observability:
- Per-feature: units_consumed, avg_latency_delta, failure_rate_when_disabled, quality_delta (if eval hooks provided).
- Per-customer: monthly units purchased vs consumed, peaks, throttled requests.
- Infra: runtime reservation failures, stale cache out-of-sync incidence.

Rollout & Experiment plan (quick):
1) Prototype runtime hook + in-memory TFF checks behind a feature flag on hosted API (2 weeks).
2) Internal dogfood: enable rerank-depth for internal accounts, measure cost/latency (2–4 weeks).
3) Add console config + billing mapping (3 weeks).
4) Beta with 3 customers and one Dedicated partner (4–8 weeks).

Success criteria:
- PMs can create and measure an experiment with TFF in < 1 day.
- For re-rank experiment: measurable quality lift >= 5% on target metric at acceptable cost (TBD).
- Runtime overhead < 2% median latency increase for enabled routes.

Open questions / risks:
- Granularity: units per feature vs units per token vs per-op? (Tradeoffs: simplicity vs precision)
- Accounting model: eventual vs strongly consistent billing — customers may demand strict accounting.
- Abuse vector: could customers exploit free credits to chain many cheap features? Need throttles.
- UX complexity: will product teams get confused by fine-grained knobs? Provide sensible presets.

Next steps (short):
- Wireframe console experience (Tess?) and sketch API (Sanjay).
- Spike runtime proof-of-concept for rerank hook (Ethan).
- Draft internal experiment template and doc the success metrics.

Notes to self: keep the primitive small and opinionated. Aim for 3 default features to start (rerank, persona_enrich, context_expand) and one extensibility hook for partners. Track real examples (customer A wanted occasional high-clarity outputs; customer B wants to reduce hallucination with a cheap verifier).

Random brainlets / implementation ideas:
- Offer prepaid bundles that map to tokens with rollover.
- Allow a per-request TTL so tokens can be reserved and applied to retries.
- Store detailed per-request TFF ledger rows in the observability pipeline (sampling to reduce cost).

End of scratch. Revisit after initial spike with numbers.
